prompted_for: "Where is the proof?" for a validation lead: standard, how we meet it, document tags (EvidenceMap)
composition: tall portrait sheet with thin outer frame
left column of 8 stacked numbered rows
middle column of short requirement labels
right column of small dog-eared document tags
layout_devices: fan of hairline connector curves from one selected row to many targets
numbered list rows 01-08 with rules between
dog-eared page-tag icons holding document codes
sheet number title block with logo
palette: deep navy text and frame lines
single steel-blue fill on active row
typography: regular grotesk list labels with numeric prefixes
line_and_texture: flat paper colour with no grain
ui_patterns: selectable list row driving a highlight
motion_implied: curves draw from the active row to its documents
selecting another row re-routes the fan
tags light up as lines arrive
t2i_prompt: Flat vector information-design sheet on warm limestone paper with a thin navy outer border and a small title block in the bottom-right corner. Bold dark navy grotesk headline top-left. Left column: a stack of numbered rows with thin rules, one row filled solid steel-blue. From the highlighted row, a fan of 1 px navy Bezier curves routes through a middle column of short labels to small dog-eared document tag icons on the right. <CONTENT>. No shadows, no gradients, generous margins, three colours only, calm traceability-diagram look.
signature_idea: Pick a standard and watch hairline wires trace it to the exact documents that prove it.
strengths: directly answers a validation lead's audit question
one accent colour does the selection job
sheet frame and title block fit the drawing-set brand idea
weaknesses: crossing curves become spaghetti when many links fan out
middle labels float without clear alignment
heavy bold headline breaks the light-headline rule
does not scale to phone width
brand_fit_why: Limestone, navy and a single steel-blue accent with square corners are on brand; bold headline and tangled curves undercut precise and calm.
